intro: Ordered so that each step removes uncertainty that later steps depend on. Nothing here is implemented by this session; each row is a proposal to be accepted or rejected by the owner. 'Fixes' rows correct a published defect that this verification pass proved; 'decisions' rows are open choices.

items.title: Re-capture and republish the Week 10 injury tables
items.why: Published counts are stale: 254 rows and 4 no-injury sections versus 279 rows and 2 sections live; Seattle and Cincinnati are shown as injury-free while listing 15 and 4 players (VR-04, VR-05, VR-06, VR-07).
items.how: Run the existing capture script, then rebuild only after the per-club row counts and the no-injury set are asserted.
items.acceptance: Every club section in the rebuilt table has the same player count as the live report, and no club shows 'No Injuries Reported' unless the page says so.
items.risk: Overwriting a good dataset with a bad parse. Mitigate by keeping the old snapshot beside the new one with its own timestamp.

items.title: Make a failed parse look different from a clean result
items.why: A zero-row club and a genuinely injury-free club render identically today; that is how Seattle and Cincinnati passed review (VQ-03).
items.how: Add explicit states no_injury_reported / not_captured / partial, render a warning badge, and fail the build on not_captured for any club that played.
items.acceptance: The build fails when a scheduled club yields zero parsed rows without a no-injury marker on the page.
items.risk: Alert fatigue if a source legitimately changes markup. Accept a documented manual override that is visible on the page.

items.title: Populate the three missing Lions game-status designations
items.why: Kerby Joseph, Cade Mays and D.J. Reed are published with a blank game-status cell while the official article lists all three as Out (VR-08, VR-12).
items.how: Capture the Week 10 injury article alongside the report page and reconcile designations by player and club, flagging conflicts instead of choosing silently.
items.acceptance: Every player listed Out/Questionable/Doubtful in the official article shows that designation, with a citation to the article.
items.risk: Article and report can disagree. Resolve by showing both with timestamps, never by averaging.

items.title: Correct the Colts depth rows and the Packers coverage error
items.why: One Colts row merges two players, another duplicates a player, and Green Bay is published as unparseable although it publishes a full text table (VR-14, VR-18, VR-19, VR-20).
items.how: Split 'Will Mallory Pharaoh Brown', drop the duplicate 'Charavarius Ward' row, add the Packers table, and change the Texans note to 'image only'.
items.acceptance: Player-name validation passes for every Colts row and the Packers club appears with its published chart.
items.risk: The source itself is an informal article list. Keep authority labelled 'club article, unofficial'.

items.title: Flag stale depth rows against the official transactions log
items.why: Baltimore still publishes Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley at QB after both went on injured reserve and a replacement was traded in (VR-17, VR-26; VQ-07).
items.how: Capture nfl.com/transactions on the same schedule as the depth pages and mark any row whose player has a later transaction.
items.acceptance: No depth row is displayed as current when a later dated transaction exists, without an explicit stale badge.
items.risk: Transaction text is free-form. Treat matching as advisory and show the matched transaction link.

items.title: Represent shared and empty depth slots faithfully
items.why: Seattle puts two players in one slot and Washington leaves a slot empty; both are currently indistinguishable from a ranked list (VR-21, VR-23; VQ-08).
items.how: Store a slot as an ordered set with explicit empty markers, and render shared slots as shared.
items.acceptance: No consumer of the data can compute 'starter = rank 1' without handling a multi-player slot.
items.risk: Changes the shape of an existing dataset. Version the schema and keep the old file readable.

items.title: Add an announced-starter evidence field (not an inferred replacement)
items.why: The blank replacement columns are correct for the report page, but the NFL does publish dated starter changes for Lock, McCord and Brissett (VR-24, VR-25; VQ-05).
items.how: New field announcement_text, announcement_url, announced_at, filled only from a dated NFL or club article, shown beside - never inside - the rank system.
items.acceptance: Every populated value links to a specific dated article, and the field is absent where no announcement exists.
items.risk: 'Expected to start' is not 'started'. Keep the wording and do not convert it to a probability.
items.source_label: NFL: Kyle McCord in line for first start

items.title: Capture the reserve list so 'not listed' never means 'available'
items.why: Malik Willis is absent from the weekly report because he is on injured reserve, not because he is healthy (VR-25; VQ-06).
items.how: Add the official reserve list to the capture set and encode availability as a tri-state: listed, not listed, on reserve.
items.acceptance: No feature can treat a reserve-list player as available.
items.risk: Reserve designations change daily. Record the capture timestamp and display it.

items.title: Promote the verification register to a build-time contract
items.why: Nothing prevents a future capture from silently breaking a claim that was verified by hand today (VQ-16).
items.how: Attach an expected value to each verified record, diff it on every capture, store results as JSON, and render failed rows as flagged rather than deleting them.
items.acceptance: A structural break in a source shows up as a failed verification row in the deployed build, not as an empty table.
items.risk: Sources legitimately change. A failure must be a prompt for review, not a build abort.

items.title: Settle the market-data decision before any line work
items.why: No originated line can be scored without permissioned historical prices and a settlement contract (VR-28; VQ-10, VQ-11).
items.how: Either obtain written terms from a provider, or formally scope the project to pre-market modelling with no ROI or leaderboard claim.
items.acceptance: A written decision exists either way; the site states which one is in force.
items.risk: Cost and terms are unknown. Choosing 'no market data' costs nothing and removes a false promise.

items.title: Pre-register the personnel ablation and its sample threshold
items.why: Without a frozen threshold, a '2nd-string dropoff' result is a fishing expedition (VQ-12, VQ-13).
items.how: Write the hypothesis, folds, grouping and minimum sample first; publish the pre-registration before any result.
items.acceptance: The pre-registration is published and dated earlier than the first result table.
items.risk: Research may conclude 'not detectable'. That is a valid, publishable outcome.
items.source_label: NIST/SEMATECH confidence limits for the mean

items.title: Label the REG9 capture by its body week, not its document title
items.why: The REG9 page's document title says Week 10 while its heading and first game say Week 9, so a citation keyed on the title mis-dates the capture (VR-02).
items.how: Store the week from the page heading and first game date, keep the raw document title as a separate field, and render both when they disagree.
items.acceptance: Any citation of REG9 shows week 9 from the heading plus the observed title text, or shows a conflict badge.
items.risk: Title text may be an NFL template bug that gets fixed later; do not hard-code the mismatch as permanent.
items.source_label: NFL official injury report, week 9 body
